from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite: The Concept of Slope"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Slope measures how steep a straight line is.",
            "- We calculate it as vertical rise over horizontal run.",
            "- On a curve, the steepness changes at every point."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a straight white line (#FFFFFF) and a simple ant shape on it.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Straight line from D1 to B6
        start_point = self.grid["D1"]
        end_point = self.grid["B6"]
        white_line = Line(start_point, end_point, color=WHITE)
        
        # Simple ant shape: Ellipse body and Dot head
        ant_body = Ellipse(width=0.3, height=0.15, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1)
        ant_head = Dot(radius=0.06, color=WHITE).next_to(ant_body, RIGHT, buff=0)
        ant = VGroup(ant_body, ant_head)
        ant.move_to(start_point)
        # Set initial orientation along the line
        line_angle = white_line.get_angle()
        ant.rotate(line_angle)
        ant.current_angle = line_angle

        self.play(Create(white_line))
        self.play(FadeIn(ant))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the 'rise' and 'run' with a green triangle (#00FF00).
        # Move the ant along the plank while the green slope triangle remains constant.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # Define triangle points on the existing line
        p1 = white_line.point_from_proportion(0.2)
        p2 = white_line.point_from_proportion(0.8)
        p_corner = np.array([p2[0], p1[1], 0])
        
        triangle = Polygon(p1, p_corner, p2, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.2, stroke_width=2)
        run_label = Text("run", color=GREEN, font_size=20).next_to(Line(p1, p_corner), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        rise_label = Text("rise", color=GREEN, font_size=20).next_to(Line(p_corner, p2), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(triangle), Write(run_label), Write(rise_label))
        
        # Move ant along the plank (line) while triangle stays constant
        self.play(ant.animate.move_to(end_point), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition to a blue curve (#0000FF). Ant walks as a white tangent line (#FFFFFF) follows.
        # Highlight slope at three points: yellow (#FFFF00), orange (#FFA500), and red (#FF0000).
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        
        # Define a blue curve spanning the right side grid area
        curve = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t, 0.6 * np.cos(t - 3) + 0.2, 0]),
            t_range=[0.5, 5.5],
            color=BLUE
        )
        
        # Tangent line that will follow the ant (initially hidden)
        tangent_line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        
        # Calculate initial curve angle for smooth transition
        # y = 0.6 * cos(t - 3) + 0.2 => y'(t) = -0.6 * sin(t - 3)
        # At t=0.5 (start), y'(0.5) = -0.6 * sin(-2.5)
        start_angle_curve = np.arctan(-0.6 * np.sin(0.5 - 3))
        
        # Transition: Fade out line/triangle elements, Create curve
        self.play(
            FadeOut(white_line), 
            FadeOut(triangle), 
            FadeOut(run_label), 
            FadeOut(rise_label),
            Create(curve),
            ant.animate.move_to(curve.point_from_proportion(0)).rotate(start_angle_curve - ant.current_angle)
        )
        ant.current_angle = start_angle_curve
        
        # Animation sequence: Ant walks along curve with tangent line
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def ant_updater(m):
            t_val = t_tracker.get_value()
            pos = curve.point_from_proportion(t_val)
            # Actual x = 0.5 + t_val * 5
            # y = 0.6 * cos(5*t_val - 2.5) + 0.2
            # dy/dt_val = -3.0 * sin(5*t_val - 2.5)
            # dx/dt_val = 5.0
            # slope = -0.6 * sin(5*t_val - 2.5)
            slope = -0.6 * np.sin(5 * t_val - 2.5)
            angle = np.arctan(slope)
            m.move_to(pos)
            m.rotate(angle - m.current_angle)
            m.current_angle = angle
            
        def tangent_updater(m):
            m.move_to(ant.get_center())
            m.set_angle(ant.current_angle)

        ant.add_updater(ant_updater)
        tangent_line.add_updater(tangent_updater)
        
        self.add(tangent_line)
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=5, rate_func=linear)
        
        # Stop dynamic movement
        ant.remove_updater(ant_updater)
        tangent_line.remove_updater(tangent_updater)
        self.play(FadeOut(tangent_line), FadeOut(ant))
        
        # Highlight slope at three distinct points on the curve
        point_proportions = [0.2, 0.5, 0.8]
        colors = [YELLOW, "#FFA500", RED]
        
        for p_prop, color in zip(point_proportions, colors):
            p_pos = curve.point_from_proportion(p_prop)
            marker_dot = Dot(p_pos, color=color)
            
            # Calculate static tangent at this specific point
            slope_val = -0.6 * np.sin(5 * p_prop - 2.5)
            marker_angle = np.arctan(slope_val)
            marker_line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=color).scale(0.7).move_to(p_pos).set_angle(marker_angle)
            
            self.play(
                FadeIn(marker_dot), 
                Create(marker_line),
                run_time=1
            )
            
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with the section title and lecture lines
        title = "Geometric Intuition: The 'Infinite Zoom'"
        lines = [
            "Zooming in on a curve reveals a surprising secret.",
            "At extreme magnification, every smooth curve looks straight.",
            "This straight line is the tangent at that point.",
            "The derivative is the slope of this tangent line.",
            "It captures the exact rate of change right now."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a red parabola (#FF0000) and mark a single point with a white dot (#FFFFFF).
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(RED))
        
        # Define the parabola y = 0.5 * x^2
        parabola = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2, x_range=[-2.5, 2.5]).set_color(RED)
        
        # We want to place a point on the curve (x=1.0, y=0.5) at grid C3
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'C3')
        
        # Shift parabola so that its point (1.0, 0.5) coincides with the dot's position
        # FunctionGraph is centered at (0, y_mid, 0) relative to its coordinates
        # So we align the point at x=1 relative to the curve's origin
        point_on_curve = np.array([1.0, 0.5, 0])
        parabola.shift(dot.get_center() - point_on_curve)
        
        self.play(Create(parabola), FadeIn(dot))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Create a magnifying glass circle around the white dot.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        mag_glass = Circle(radius=0.7, color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        mag_glass.move_to(dot.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(mag_glass))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Zoom into the area inside the circle. The red curve should gradually appear flatter until it looks like a straight line.
        # Overlay a green tangent line (#00FF00).
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        
        # Scaling group relative to the dot at C3
        zoom_group = VGroup(parabola, dot)
        
        # Pre-calculate tangent line at x=1 for y=0.5*x^2 (slope = 1.0)
        # It should pass through the dot's center
        tangent_line = Line(start=LEFT*2, end=RIGHT*2, color=GREEN)
        tangent_line.rotate(np.arctan(1.0)) 
        tangent_line.move_to(dot.get_center())
        
        # Zoom animation
        self.play(
            zoom_group.animate.scale(10, about_point=dot.get_center()),
            parabola.animate.set_stroke(width=2), # Prevent line from becoming too thick
            run_time=3
        )
        
        self.play(Create(tangent_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Display the text 'Instantaneous Slope' in white (#FFFFFF) next to the zoomed-in line.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        slope_label = Text("Instantaneous Slope", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        # Position near the zoomed view, around D4/E4 area
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, 'D4')
        
        self.play(Write(slope_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # It captures the exact rate of change right now.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Visual emphasis on the dot/point of tangency
        self.play(
            Indicate(dot, color=WHITE, scale_factor=1.5),
            Flash(dot, color=WHITE, line_length=0.2)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching content from shared state (already confirmed)
        title_text = "The Power Rule: Expanding Dimensions"
        lecture_lines = [
            "The power rule calculates derivatives for functions like x squared.",
            "Imagine a square growing by a tiny amount of area.",
            "Growth happens along the boundary of the existing shape.",
            "For x squared, the rate of growth is two x.",
            "Power rule: drop the exponent and subtract one."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        BLUE_SQ = "#0000FF"
        WHITE_TXT = "#FFFFFF"
        GREEN_STRIP = "#00FF00"
        YELLOW_LBL = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # The power rule calculates derivatives for functions like x squared.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE_SQ)
        
        square = Square(side_length=1.0, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=BLUE_SQ, stroke_color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'D3', scale_factor=2.0)
        
        label_x_left = MathTex("x", color=WHITE_TXT)
        self.place_at_grid(label_x_left, 'D2')
        
        label_x_bottom = MathTex("x", color=WHITE_TXT)
        self.place_at_grid(label_x_bottom, 'E3')
        
        area_text = MathTex("x^2", color=WHITE_TXT)
        self.place_at_grid(area_text, 'D3')
        
        self.play(
            Create(square),
            Write(label_x_left),
            Write(label_x_bottom),
            Write(area_text),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Imagine a square growing by a tiny amount of area.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN_STRIP)
        
        # Grid C3 is at the top edge of square at D3
        top_strip = Rectangle(width=2.0, height=0.2, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=GREEN_STRIP, stroke_color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(top_strip, 'C3')
        top_strip.shift(UP * 0.1) # Align outside top edge
        
        # Grid D4 is at the right edge of square at D3
        right_strip = Rectangle(width=0.2, height=2.0, fill_opacity=0.8, fill_color=GREEN_STRIP, stroke_color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(right_strip, 'D4')
        right_strip.shift(RIGHT * 0.1) # Align outside right edge
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(top_strip),
            FadeIn(right_strip),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.place_at_grid(label_strip_top, 'B3')
        
        label_strip_right = MathTex("x", color=YELLOW_LBL)
        self.place_at_grid(label_strip_right, 'D5')
        
        self.play(
            Write(label_strip_top),
            Write(label_strip_right),
            run_time=1.0
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # For x squared, the rate of growth is two x.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE_TXT)
        
        # Target 2x label
        target_2x = MathTex("2x", color=WHITE_TXT)
        self.place_at_grid(target_2x, 'C5')
        
        # Main formula

        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A2', 'A5', scale_factor=1.2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Trigonometric Intuition: The Unit Circle Dance"
        lines = [
            "Imagine a point moving around a unit circle.",
            "The height of the point represents the sine function.",
            "Its vertical speed depends on its horizontal position.",
            "When height changes fastest, horizontal value is highest.",
            "This proves the derivative of sine is cosine."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Assets/Values
        theta = ValueTracker(0.0)
        radius = 1.5
        
        # Colors for matching lecture lines
        COLOR_SIN = "#0000FF"
        COLOR_COS = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_FASTEST = "#00FFFF"
        
        # Grid center for the unit circle (Area B2 to E5)
        # B2: (1.5, 1.2), E5: (4.5, -1.8) -> center (3.0, -0.3)
        circle_center = np.array([3.0, -0.3, 0])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Imagine a point moving around a unit circle.
        unit_circle = Circle(radius=radius, color=WHITE)
        unit_circle.move_to(circle_center)
        
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
        dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(
            circle_center + np.array([radius * np.cos(theta.get_value()), radius * np.sin(theta.get_value()), 0])
        ))
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            Create(unit_circle),
            FadeIn(dot)
        )
        self.play(theta.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # The height of the point represents the sine function.
        blue_line = Line(color=COLOR_SIN)
        blue_line.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([
            circle_center + np.array([radius * np.cos(theta.get_value()), 0, 0]),
            circle_center + np.array([radius * np.cos(theta.get_value()), radius * np.sin(theta.get_value()), 0])
        ]))
        
        sin_label = MathTex(r"\sin(x)", color=COLOR_SIN, font_size=24)
        sin_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(blue_line, RIGHT, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_SIN),
            Create(blue_line),
            FadeIn(sin_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Its vertical speed depends on its horizontal position.
        red_line = Line(color=COLOR_COS)
        red_line.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_points_as_corners([
            circle_center,
            circle_center + np.array([radius * np.cos(theta.get_value()), 0, 0])
        ]))
        
        cos_label = MathTex(r"\cos(x)", color=COLOR_COS, font_size=24)
        cos_label.add_updater(lambda l: l.next_to(red_line, DOWN, buff=0.1))

        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_COS),
            Create(red_line),
            FadeIn(cos_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # When height changes fastest, horizontal value is highest.
        def get_flash_anim(pos, color):
            f = Circle(radius=0.1, color=color, stroke_width=6).move_to(pos)
            return AnimationGroup(
                f.animate.scale(6).set_stroke(opacity=0),
                run_time=0.6,
                rate_func=linear
            )

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with the specific title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Application: The Cheetah’s Sprint",
            [
                "Derivatives describe real movement, like a running cheetah.",
                "Velocity is the derivative of position over time.",
                "Acceleration is the derivative of velocity, measuring speed changes."
            ]
        )
        
        # Define colors for consistency between text and visuals
        COLOR_POS = "#58ACFA" # Light Blue
        COLOR_VEL = "#58FA58" # Light Green
        COLOR_ACC = "#FA5858" # Light Red
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_POS))
        
        # Cheetah representation (using a simple triangle)
        cheetah = Triangle(color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=1).rotate(-PI/2)
        self.place_at_grid(cheetah, "B1", scale_factor=0.3)
        
        # Position label s(t) that follows the cheetah
        pos_label = MathTex("s(t)", color=COLOR_POS)
        pos_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(cheetah, UP, buff=0.2))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(cheetah), FadeIn(pos_label))
        
        # Move cheetah from start to end of track (B1 to B6)
        dest_pos_end = self.grid["B6"]
        self.play(cheetah.animate.move_to(dest_pos_end), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transition highlight to second line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_VEL)
        )
        
        # Velocity formula positioned in grid
        vel_formula = MathTex("v(t) = s'(t)", color=COLOR_VEL)
        self.place_at_grid(vel_formula, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Speedometer setup
        speedo_center = self.grid["E2"]
        speedo_arc = Arc(radius=0.7, start_angle=PI, angle=-PI, color=WHITE)
        speedo_arc.move_to(speedo_center)
        arc_center_point = speedo_arc.get_arc_center()
        
        # Needle and ValueTracker for synchronized speed display
        vt = ValueTracker(0)
        needle = Line(arc_center_point, arc_center_point + LEFT * 0.6, color=COLOR_VEL)
        
        def update_needle(m):
            angle = (1 - vt.get_value()) * PI
            new_end = arc_center_point + np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0]) * 0.6
            m.set_points_as_corners([arc_center_point, new_end])
            
        needle.add_updater(update_needle)
        
        speedo_text = Text("Velocity", font_size=16, color=COLOR_VEL)
        speedo_text.next_to(speedo_arc, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(
            Create(speedo_arc),
            Create(needle),
            Write(vel_formula),
            FadeIn(speedo_text)
        )
        
        # Demonstrate variable velocity: reset and move again
        self.play(
            cheetah.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]), 
            vt.animate.set_value(0), 
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Move with acceleration/deceleration rate_func
        self.play(
            cheetah.animate.move_to(dest_pos_end),
            vt.animate.set_value(1),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=slow_into 
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition highlight to third line
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_ACC)
        )
        
        # Acceleration formula
        acc_formula = MathTex("a(t) = v'(t)", color=COLOR_ACC)
        self.place_at_grid(acc_formula, "C4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Acceleration arrow and label following the cheetah
        acc_arrow = Arrow(LEFT, RIGHT, color=COLOR_ACC, buff=0, stroke_width=4)
        acc_label = Text("Acceleration", font_size=16, color=COLOR_ACC)
        
        acc_arrow.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(cheetah, RIGHT, buff=0.1))
        acc_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(acc_arrow, UP, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(Write(acc_formula), GrowArrow(acc_arrow), FadeIn(acc_label))
        
        # Final sprint showing high acceleration
        self.play(
            cheetah.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]),
            vt.animate.set_value(0),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.play(
            cheetah.animate.move_to(dest_pos_end),
            vt.animate.set_value(1),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=rush_into # High acceleration profile
        )
        
        # Pulse animation for labels at top speed/acceleration
        self.play(
            speedo_text.animate.scale(1.3).set_color(WHITE),
            acc_label.animate.scale(1.3).set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=0.3
        )
        self.play(
            speedo_text.animate.scale(1/1.3).set_color(COLOR_VEL),
            acc_label.animate.scale(1/1.3).set_color(COLOR_ACC),
            run_time=0.3
        )
        self.play(
            speedo_text.animate.scale(1.3).set_color(WHITE),
            acc_label.animate.scale(1.3).set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=0.3
        )
        self.play(
            speedo_text.animate.scale(1/1.3).set_color(COLOR_VEL),
            acc_label.animate.scale(1/1.3).set_color(COLOR_ACC),
            run_time=0.3
        )

        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Calculus turns geometry into precise mathematical formulas.",
            "Derivatives give us a shortcut to understand change.",
            "Now you can see the rhythm in the world's movement."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary: The Calculus Lens", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a split-screen effect. 
        # On the left (of grid area), display white formulas (#FFFFFF): 'd/dx x^n' and 'd/dx sin x'.
        # On the right (of grid area), show a gold path (#FFD700) of a soaring eagle.
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        formula1 = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx} x^n = n x^{n-1}", color=WHITE)
        formula2 = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx} \sin x = \cos x", color=WHITE)
        formulas = VGroup(formula1, formula2).arrange(DOWN, buff=1.0)
        
        # Place formulas in the left half of the grid (Cols 1-3)
        self.place_in_area(formulas, 'B1', 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Eagle path (ParametricFunction)
        # Using a simple curved path to represent a soaring eagle
        path = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t, 0.5 * np.sin(2*t) + 0.3 * t**2, 0]),
            t_range=[-1.5, 1.5],
            color="#FFD700"
        )
        # Place path in the right half of the grid (Cols 4-6)
        self.place_in_area(path, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formulas), Create(path))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw tangent lines on the eagle's path that change color to match the corresponding formulas on the left.
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Create tangent line with ValueTracker
        t_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        tangent_line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE).scale(0.6)
        
        def update_tangent(mob):
            t = t_tracker.get_value()
            p = path.point_from_proportion(t)
            dt = 0.001
            if t + dt <= 1:
                p_next = path.point_from_proportion(t + dt)
                direction = p_next - p
            else:
                p_prev = path.point_from_proportion(t - dt)
                direction = p - p_prev
            
            direction_norm = np.linalg.norm(direction)
            if direction_norm > 0:
                direction /= direction_norm
            
            mob.move_to(p)
            angle = np.arctan2(direction[1], direction[0])
            mob.set_angle(angle)

        tangent_line.add_updater(update_tangent)
        
        self.add(tangent_line)
        # Move along path. Storyboard mentions tangent lines change color. 
        # Since formulas are white, we keep it white. 
        # But let's animate the path and the line moving.
        self.play(t_tracker.animate.set_value(1), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition both sides to merge into a single green text (#00FF00): 'The Language of Change'.
        
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        final_text = Text("The Language of Change", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_in_area(final_text, 'B1', 'E6', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        tangent_line.clear_updaters()
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(formulas),
            FadeOut(path),
            FadeOut(tangent_line),
            Write(final_text)
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Rhythm of Change: Derivative Formulas and Geometric Intuition
outline.target_audience: Introductory Calculus Students (High School or First-Year University)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Slope
sections.content: Establish the foundation of 'Rate of Change' by reviewing the slope of a straight line (rise/run). Transition from a constant slope to the idea of a changing slope on a curve.
sections.example: An ant walking up a straight plank (constant slope) vs. the same ant walking over a smooth, round pebble (changing slope).

sections.title: Geometric Intuition: The 'Infinite Zoom'
sections.content: Introduce the derivative as the 'instantaneous' slope. Use the geometric concept of a tangent line. Visualize 'local linearity'—as we zoom into a point on a curve, the curve starts to look like a straight line.
sections.example: A magnifying glass zooming into a point on a parabola. At 100x zoom, the curve is indistinguishable from its tangent line, representing the derivative at that specific point.

sections.title: The Power Rule: Expanding Dimensions
sections.content: Introduce the formula d/dx(x^n) = nx^(n-1). Explain the geometric logic: the derivative of an area (x^2) is the perimeter/boundary (2x) that allows it to grow.
sections.example: A square robot that grows by adding thin strips to its edges. If its area is x², the 'extra' bit it grows by at any moment is proportional to its 2 sides (2x).

sections.title: Trigonometric Intuition: The Unit Circle Dance
sections.content: Derive why d/dx(sin x) = cos x. Use the unit circle to show that the rate of vertical change (sine) is exactly the horizontal position (cosine) at any given angle.
sections.example: A Ferris wheel passenger. When they are at the very side (sin x = 0), they are moving vertically at their fastest (cos x = 1). At the top (sin x = 1), their vertical movement stops for a split second (cos x = 0).

sections.title: Application: The Cheetah’s Sprint
sections.content: Connect formulas to real-world motion. Explain the hierarchy: Position ➔ Velocity (1st derivative) ➔ Acceleration (2nd derivative). Show how these formulas predict physical limits.
sections.example: A robotic cheetah chasing a drone. We use the power rule on its position formula to find its speedometer reading (velocity) and the derivative of that to find the 'jerk' or kick of its motors (acceleration).

sections.title: Summary: The Calculus Lens
sections.content: Recap the connection between the 'formula' and the 'shape'. Emphasize that the derivative formula is just a shortcut to describe the 'steepness' of the world's movements.
sections.example: A split-screen view: on the left, the equations (d/dx); on the right, the curving path of a soaring eagle, perfectly synchronized.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Slope
lecture_lines: Slope measures how steep a straight line is.
We calculate it as vertical rise over horizontal run.
On a curve, the steepness changes at every point.
animations: Create a straight white line (#FFFFFF) using and place on it, set against. Highlight the 'rise' and 'run' with a green triangle (#00FF00).
Move along the plank while the green slope triangle remains constant in shape and color.
Transition to. walks along it as follows as a white tangent line (#FFFFFF), changing its angle.
Highlight the slope at three distinct points on the curve using in yellow (#FFFF00), orange (#FFA500), and red (#FF0000) to show change.

storyboard.title: Geometric Intuition: The 'Infinite Zoom'
lecture_lines: Zooming in on a curve reveals a surprising secret.
At extreme magnification, every smooth curve looks straight.
This straight line is the tangent at that point.
The derivative is the slope of this tangent line.
It captures the exact rate of change right now.
animations: Draw a red parabola (#FF0000) and mark a single point with a white dot (#FFFFFF).
Create a magnifying glass circle around the white dot.
Zoom into the area inside the circle. The red curve should gradually appear flatter until it looks like a straight line.
Overlay a green tangent line (#00FF00) on the flattened curve to demonstrate 'local linearity'.
Display the text 'Instantaneous Slope' in white (#FFFFFF) next to the zoomed-in line.

storyboard.title: The Power Rule: Expanding Dimensions
lecture_lines: The power rule calculates derivatives for functions like x squared.
Imagine a square growing by a tiny amount of area.
Growth happens along the boundary of the existing shape.
For x squared, the rate of growth is two x.
Power rule: drop the exponent and subtract one.
animations: Draw a blue square (#0000FF) with side labels 'x' and area text 'x^2' in white (#FFFFFF).
Animate the square growing by adding two thin green strips (#00FF00) to the top and right edges.
Label each green strip as 'x' in yellow (#FFFF00) and show them merging to represent '2x'.
Fade in the formula 'd/dx(x^2) = 2x' in white (#FFFFFF) at the top of the screen.
Flash the '2x' and the green strips simultaneously to emphasize their relationship.

storyboard.title: Trigonometric Intuition: The Unit Circle Dance
lecture_lines: Imagine a point moving around a unit circle.
The height of the point represents the sine function.
Its vertical speed depends on its horizontal position.
When height changes fastest, horizontal value is highest.
This proves the derivative of sine is cosine.
animations: Draw a white unit circle (#FFFFFF) with a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/point.svg] rotating counter-clockwise.
Show a vertical blue line (#0000FF) representing 'sin x' (height) and a horizontal red line (#FF0000) representing 'cos x'.
As the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/point.svg] reaches the side, the blue line grows fastest; highlight this with a cyan flash (#00FFFF).
As the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/point.svg] reaches the top, the blue line stops growing; highlight the horizontal red line (cos x = 0) with a red flash (#FF0000).
Display 'd/dx(sin x) = cos x' in white (#FFFFFF) centered in the circle.

storyboard.title: Application: The Cheetah’s Sprint
lecture_lines: Derivatives describe real movement, like a running cheetah.
Velocity is the derivative of position over time.
Acceleration is the derivative of velocity, measuring speed changes.
animations: Show a simple cheetah icon moving across the screen from left to right.
Display the position formula 's(t)' in blue (#0000FF) above the cheetah.
Draw a green speedometer (#00FF00) that shows the velocity 'v(t)' as the derivative of 's(t)'.
As the cheetah accelerates, show a red vector arrow (#FF0000) for acceleration 'a(t)'.
Pulse the labels 'Velocity' and 'Acceleration' in their respective colors as the cheetah reaches top speed.

storyboard.title: Summary: The Calculus Lens
lecture_lines: Calculus turns geometry into precise mathematical formulas.
Derivatives give us a shortcut to understand change.
Now you can see the rhythm in the world's movement.
animations: Create a split-screen effect. On the left, display white formulas (#FFFFFF): 'd/dx x^n' and 'd/dx sin x'.
On the right, show a gold path (#FFD700) of a soaring eagle [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/eagle.svg].
Draw tangent lines on the eagle [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/eagle.svg] path that change color to match the corresponding formulas on the left.
Transition both sides to merge into a single green text (#00FF00): 'The Language of Change'.
